q: The architect was commissioned by a friend to design a townhouse project and was specifically asked to prepare feasibility studies and marketing posters. When should the architect be paid?
n: For a discrete set of studies and posters, the architect is paid once the work is submitted, as the agreement sets. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 201.

q: Cost-based method employed for non-creative works.
n: A multiple of direct personnel expense pays the architect's staff salaries times a multiplier for overhead and profit. It is cost-based, so it suits non-creative, time-driven work such as studies and inventories. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202 (MDPE).

q: What is the general basis of the architect's minimum basic fee?
n: The minimum basic fee is set by the type of structure. The SPP groups buildings by complexity (Groups 1–7), and each group has its own fee percentage. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.

q: What should NOT be a basis of the architect's fee?
n: Fees rest on the scope, complexity, skill and documents required, never on personal relationships. Friendship-based discounting undercuts the profession. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct; 2016 Architect's Guidelines.

q: An architect was hired by a client to design a condominium located in a commercial area, but no formal contract was signed. After several meetings, the architect produced a schematic design, which was subsequently approved. However, the client decided to no longer proceed with the architect. How much compensation is the architect entitled to?
o: 15% of contract price plus 5% for breach of contract
n: Without a signed service agreement the architect has no contractual fee to enforce, which is why the SPP insists on a written agreement before design work. He might still claim the reasonable value of work under quasi-contract. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202; Civil Code, Art. 2142.

q: An architect was commissioned to design a residential project with a contract stipulating full payment upon completion of construction. Everything worked out until the project was finished, but the owner ran out of budget to start the construction. How much is the architect entitled to collect legally?
n: By the end of contract documents the architect has earned 90% of the fee (5 + 15 + 20 + 50). He can collect that legally even if construction never starts. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: Aclient is very happy with the design plans made for his house. He decides to use the same design for his son's house. How much will the client pay the architect for the second house?
n: The older UAP SPP charged 60% of the fee for re-using a house design without changes. The 2016 Guidelines now charge 50% for the second building, 40% for the third and 30% for later ones. Of the choices, 60% matches the older schedule. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Group 6 (repetitive construction).

q: If the client decides to hire the architect for Design-Build by administration, how much additional fee should the architect charge in addition to the original 10%?
n: For design-build by administration, the recommended fee is 7% of PCC, on top of the architect's regular design services fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.4.1.

q: What is the compensation for long-term relations in a project?
n: For a long-term relationship on a project, compensation by professional fee plus expenses (a fixed fee plus reimbursables) is used. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: What method of compensation has a continuing relationship with the architect?
n: Professional fee plus expenses suits a continuing relationship with the architect over time. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: What method of payment is used where there is a continuing relationship involving a series of projects?
n: For a continuing relationship over a series of projects, the SPP uses a retainer (or professional fee plus expenses), which is not among the choices, so "none of the above" is correct. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines (methods of compensation).

q: How is a building and facilities administration architect paid?
o: Percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees
n: A building and facilities administration architect is paid a percentage of gross rentals, maintenance and security fees (value-pricing, 4–6%). Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.1.

q: How many percent should the Architect be compensated after the Contract Document Phase even if the project has not commenced?
n: After contract documents the architect has earned 90% of the professional fee, not a percentage of PCC, so none of the listed PCC figures is right. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: A project is on hold for a year for lack of funds. When should you bill for the contract documents?
n: The contract documents fee is billed on submission of the documents, before construction, even if the project is put on hold. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.4.

q: What is the basis of the Building Administration fee?
o: Percentage of gross rentals, maintenance, and security fees
n: A building administrator can be paid a percentage of gross rentals and fees, a monthly salary or fee, MDPE, a retainer or professional fee plus expenses, so all of the above. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 205, Sec. 10.2.

q: Design build by maximum cost, how much is the architect remunerated?
o: Built in the max cost exclusive of architectural registration fee
Lump sum inclusive of architectural fee
n: For design-build on a guaranteed maximum cost, the architect's remuneration is built into the maximum cost, separate from the architectural fee. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 207, Sec. 12.3.

q: How much is the Minimum basic fee from the PCC for Simple Projects without partitions, such as Hangars?
n: Simple projects without partitions, such as hangars, are Group 1, with a recommended DAEDS fee of 5% of PCC. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Sec. 6.3.1.

q: For repetitive designs, what is the fee for each unit after the third?
n: For repeated designs the 2016 Guidelines charge 30% of the fee for the fourth and later buildings, so 40%, 50% and 60% are all wrong. Source: 2016 Architect's Guidelines, SPP Doc. 202, Group 6.

q: When is the Professional Tax Receipt due each year?
n: The Professional Tax Receipt is paid to the LGU on or before January 31 each year. Source: RA 7160 (Local Government Code), Sec. 139.

q: In which month are business permits usually renewed?
n: Business permits (mayor's permits) are renewed in January, the first 20 days of the year. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 165–167; LGU revenue codes.

q: What is the first step in renewing a business permit?
n: Business permit renewal starts with the barangay business clearance, which the LGU requires before the mayor's permit. Source: RA 7160, Sec. 152(c).

q: When is the annual income tax return due?
n: Annual income tax returns of calendar-year filers are due on April 15. Source: NIRC (RA 8424 as amended by TRAIN, RA 10963), Sec. 51.

q: What is the standard VAT rate in the Philippines?
n: The standard VAT rate in the Philippines is 12%. VAT is charged on the sale of goods and services by VAT-registered persons. Some sales are zero-rated or exempt. Source: NIRC, Sec. 106 (as amended by RA 9337).

q: Under OSHS Rule 1033, how many full-time safety officers does a hazardous workplace with 51–200 workers need at minimum?
n: For a hazardous workplace with 51–200 workers, OSHS Rule 1033 requires at least one full-time safety officer. Source: DOLE OSHS Rule 1033; DO 198-18.

q: An owner authorizes the architect to act for him through a:
n: An owner authorizes the architect to act for him on specific matters (such as permit processing) through a special power of attorney. Source: Civil Code of the Philippines, Art. 1878.

q: As per the LGU code, the maximum amount a professional can pay for their Community Tax Certificate (CEDULA) io, 2.
n: The community tax for individuals is ₱5 basic plus ₱1 per ₱1,000 of income, capped at ₱5,000. Source: RA 7160 (Local Government Code), Sec. 157.

q: For a replacement PRC ID, besides the fee, you must present a:
n: To replace a lost PRC ID you present a notarized affidavit of loss, besides paying the fee. Source: PRC Citizen's Charter (replacement of lost ID).

q: As an Architect, you have a responsibility to your staff and fellow architects. Which of the following would best show this?
o: Be an example of how to become a good professional
Train them to be good in their profession
n: An architect's duty to staff and colleagues is best shown by training and mentoring them to grow in the profession. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct (duties to colleagues and subordinates).

q: How should an architect compensate subordinates?
n: Subordinates should be paid fairly, commensurate with their work. Source: PRBOA Code of Ethical Conduct; Labor Code of the Philippines.

q: For the registration of an architectural corporation, where would you go first?
n: An architectural corporation is first registered with the SEC as a juridical entity, then with the PRC and Board. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 37; RA 11232 (Revised Corporation Code).

q: If planning to set up a corporation before going to SEC, where should you get an endorsement?
n: Before the SEC registers a professional corporation, it needs a PRC endorsement or clearance confirming its professional members. Source: SEC requirements for professional corporations; RA 9266, Sec. 37.

q: What advantage does 3D and computer graphics give architects and clients?
n: 3D modelling and computer graphics give efficient production and realistic visualization, so clients understand the design before it is built. Source: Kalay, Architecture's New Media (MIT Press).

q: What is the size of the basic drawing submitted to the OBO for Building Permit applications?
n: Permit drawings are commonly submitted on A1-size sheets, close to the 20 × 30 in format. Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302 (sheet sizes); OBO practice.

q: The architect has chosen a winning bidder, but the owner doesn't approve. What is the architect's course of action?
n: The owner decides the award. If he rejects the recommended bidder and no agreement is reached, the proper step is to re-bid the project. Source: RA 9184 IRR, Sec. 35 (failure of bidding); UAP SPP Doc. 202 (bidding).

q: What must be the character of an architect nowadays?
n: Today's architect must be flexible in design, adapting to changing client needs, technology and sustainability demands. Source: UAP SPP Doc. 200 series (the architect's role).

q: After passing the LEA, what should the new architect do?
n: After passing the LEA, the new architect prepares for the oath-taking, then registers to receive the COR and PIC. Source: RA 9266, Sec. 17–18.

q: What is the standard size of architectural drawings?
n: Philippine architectural working drawings are commonly 20 × 30 in (about 500 × 760 mm). Source: NBC (PD 1096) IRR, Rule III, Sec. 302; Philippine drafting practice.

q: What scale or full-size model is used for teaching, demonstration, evaluation or promotion?
n: A mock-up is a scale or full-size model used for teaching, demonstration, evaluation or promotion. Source: Ching, A Visual Dictionary of Architecture.
